strings.d1.s0.name: Hawa Mahal
strings.d1.s0.tips: The Palace of Winds has 953 windows. Morning light hits the facade; shoot it from the café opposite (Wind View).
strings.d1.s1.name: City Palace Jaipur
strings.d1.s1.tips: The maharaja's palace, now a museum. Look for the four seasonal gates in the Pritam Niwas courtyard.
strings.d1.s2.name: Jantar Mantar Jaipur
strings.d1.s2.tips: A giant stone observatory with a 27 m sundial. UNESCO listed.
strings.d1.s3.name: Laxmi Misthan Bhandar
strings.d1.s3.tips: On Johari Bazaar since 1727. Try dal baati churma, ghewar and pyaz kachori.
strings.d1.s4.name: Johari Bazaar
strings.d1.s4.tips: Jewellery and block-printed fabrics. Haggle, and note the shops are shaded in the midday heat.
strings.d1.b0.name: Rawat Misthan Bhandar
strings.d1.b0.tips: Pyaz kachori, a classic street snack.
strings.d1.b1.name: Albert Hall Museum
strings.d1.b1.tips: An Indo-Saracenic museum. Air-conditioned, and lit up at night.
strings.d2.s0.name: Amber Fort
strings.d2.s0.tips: A Rajput hilltop fort with the Sheesh Mahal (mirror palace). Take a jeep instead of an elephant, and arrive at the 08:00 opening while it's cool.
strings.d2.s1.name: Panna Meena ka Kund
strings.d2.s1.tips: A stepwell below Amber, ideal for symmetrical photos.
strings.d2.s2.name: Jaigarh Fort
strings.d2.s2.tips: Home to Jaivana, the world's largest wheeled cannon. It sits above Amber.
strings.d2.s3.name: 1135 AD Amber Fort Restaurant
strings.d2.s3.tips: A royal thali served on silver plates inside the fort.
strings.d2.s4.name: Nahargarh Fort
strings.d2.s4.tips: A fort looking down over the city. Watch the sunset and the Pink City lights from the Padao café.
strings.d2.b0.name: Samode Haveli Restaurant
strings.d2.b0.tips: Lunch in a haveli, instead of the fort.
strings.d2.b1.name: Jal Mahal
strings.d2.b1.tips: A palace in the middle of a lake. View it from the shore at sunset, instead of Nahargarh.
strings.d3.s0.name: Galtaji Monkey Temple
strings.d3.s0.tips: Sacred pools and monkeys in a valley. Cool in the morning; cameras cost 200 INR.
strings.d3.s1.name: Birla Mandir Jaipur
strings.d3.s1.tips: A white marble Lakshmi Narayan temple.
strings.d3.s2.name: Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing
strings.d3.s2.tips: A block-printing museum in Amber, with a workshop demonstration.
strings.d3.s3.name: Anokhi Cafe Jaipur
strings.d3.s3.tips: An organic café below the block-print shop.
strings.d3.s4.name: Sanganer Block Printing Workshops
strings.d3.s4.tips: Jaipur's printing village, with fabric and paper workshops. Buy direct from the makers.
strings.d3.b0.name: Tapri Central Jaipur
strings.d3.b0.tips: A rooftop tea house serving chai and bun maska.
strings.d3.b1.name: Patrika Gate
strings.d3.b1.tips: A brightly painted gate at Jawahar Circle, instead of Sanganer.
strings.d4.s0.name: Pushkar Lake Ghats
strings.d4.s0.tips: 2.5 hours from Jaipur. A sacred lake with 52 ghats; go barefoot and beware of flower sellers.
strings.d4.s1.name: Brahma Temple Pushkar
strings.d4.s1.tips: One of the world's few temples to Brahma, in blue and white.
strings.d4.s2.name: Pushkar Bazaar
strings.d4.s2.tips: A hippie bazaar selling leather, silver and music.
strings.d4.s3.name: Sunset Cafe Pushkar
strings.d4.s3.tips: A lakeside café serving vegetarian food (no meat or alcohol in Pushkar), including falafel.
strings.d4.s4.name: Savitri Temple Ropeway
strings.d4.s4.tips: Take the cable car up to the hilltop temple for views of the lake and desert at sunset. A camel safari is optional.
strings.d4.b0.name: Honey & Spice Pushkar
strings.d4.b1.name: Pushkar Camel Safari
strings.d4.b1.tips: Ride a camel across the dunes at sunset, instead of the temple.
strings.d5.s0.name: Ranthambore National Park Safari
strings.d5.s0.tips: 3.5 hours from Jaipur (staying one night is ideal). Morning jeep safari; tiger zones 1-5. Book online 3 months ahead.
strings.d5.s1.name: Ranthambore Fort
strings.d5.s1.tips: A 10th-century fort inside the park, with a Ganesh temple and lake views.
strings.d5.s2.name: Ranthambore Dhaba Lunch
strings.d5.s2.tips: A dhaba (roadside eatery) in Sawai Madhopur serving dal and roti.
strings.d5.s3.name: Dastkar Ranthambore
strings.d5.s3.tips: Handicrafts from a women's cooperative, including tiger-print textiles.
strings.d5.b0.name: Ranthambore Afternoon Safari
strings.d5.b0.tips: A second chance to spot a tiger, instead of shopping.
strings.d5.b1.name: Sawai Madhopur Station Canteen
strings.d5.b1.tips: A meal at the railway station.
strings.d6.s0.name: Govind Dev Ji Temple
strings.d6.s0.tips: A Krishna temple in the City Palace gardens. The morning aarti (worship ceremony) is crowded and lively.
strings.d6.s1.name: Bapu Bazaar
strings.d6.s1.tips: Jaipur's market for textiles and mojari (leather slippers). Haggle.
strings.d6.s2.name: Masala Chowk
strings.d6.s2.tips: An open-air local food court in the Ram Niwas gardens, serving pani puri and pav bhaji.
strings.d6.s3.name: Hawa Mahal Rooftop Cafés
strings.d6.s3.tips: Have sunset tea with a view of Hawa Mahal from the Tattoo Cafe rooftop.
strings.d6.s4.name: Chokhi Dhani
strings.d6.s4.tips: A Rajasthani village-themed evening with puppets, camels and unlimited dal baati (20 km from the city).
strings.d6.b0.name: Peacock Rooftop Pearl Palace
strings.d6.b0.tips: A rooftop restaurant, instead of the village park.
strings.d6.b1.name: Jawahar Kala Kendra
strings.d6.b1.tips: Correa's arts centre, with exhibitions. Go instead of the bazaar.
strings.d7.theme: Block prints and a gentle goodbye
strings.d7.s0.name: Rambagh Palace Gardens
strings.d7.s0.tips: The gardens of the palace hotel, with peacocks. Breakfast or tea here is expensive.
strings.d7.s1.name: Anokhi Café Jaipur
strings.d7.s1.tips: An organic café and block-print shop. Have a farewell breakfast.
strings.d7.s2.name: Jaipur Modern
strings.d7.s3.name: Jaipur Airport
strings.d7.s3.tips: The airport is 30 minutes away. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Sahu Chai Wala
strings.d7.b0.tips: Legendary street chai on Chaura Rasta. Have a farewell cup.
strings.d7.b1.name: Ram Niwas Garden
strings.d7.b1.tips: The garden around Albert Hall, instead of the shop.
strings.note0: In Jaipur, use auto-rickshaws and Uber; hire a car for the day for the forts (~2,500 INR). The composite ticket (1,500 INR for foreigners) covers 8 monuments over 2 days.
strings.note1: June to September brings 40°C heat and the monsoon: plan sightseeing for 08:00-12:00 and after 16:00, and visit palaces and museums at midday. October to March is ideal (20-28°C); mornings can be foggy from November to January.
strings.note2: Try dal baati churma, pyaz kachori, ghewar and lassi. There is no meat or alcohol in Pushkar. Tip 10%.
strings.note3: Monument entry costs foreigners 200-1,000 INR. Amber is cool and empty at 08:00; take a jeep instead of an elephant ride.
strings.note4: Book the Ranthambore safari online 3 months ahead (tiger zones 1-5). Staying one night isn't essential for the safari, but it's more comfortable.
strings.note5: Haggle: aim for a third of the first price. Buy block-printed fabric from the makers in Sanganer.
